reading: Each of the two colours has two objects. The objects are regrouped into one column per colour (columns packed from the left in order of each colour's leftmost x, one empty column between). In each column the objects stack upward from the bottom row with one empty row between them, left-aligned, the object with the smaller leftmost x at the bottom.

slots.unit: each single-colour object (8-connected), keeping its shape
slots.group: objects of the same colour form one column; columns ordered by the colour's leftmost input x, packed from x=0 with a 1-column gap (column width = widest object)
slots.order: inside a column, objects sorted by leftmost input x; first one sits on the bottom row, next one above it with a 1-row gap; all left-aligned to the column's x

why: every output object is an input object translated; per colour they are stacked bottom-up, gap 1, ordered by input leftmost x

reading: The grid is a 3x3 array of panels separated by lines. Each panel holds a small mark pattern pointing toward one of the 9 positions (the off-centre direction of its marks); every panel is moved to the panel slot its pattern points at, and the symmetric pattern goes to the centre.

slots.unit: each of the 9 panels (cut by the full separator lines)
slots.key: sign of (centroid of the panel's non-background cells minus the panel centre), per axis, gives the target slot in the 3x3 panel array; centroid at the centre -> centre slot

why: each output panel equals the input panel whose marks point toward that slot; the 9 directions form a permutation

reading: Cut the grid recursively into panels by full separator lines. A panel split by a colour-4 line is mirrored across that line (its two halves swap). A panel with no 4 line that holds colour 1 plus one other block colour has its 1 blocks recoloured to that other colour.

slots.scale: panels cut recursively by full one-colour lines (5/7/9 lines divide; inside a panel, a full 4 line is the swap axis)
slots.swap: panel containing a full 4 line: reflect the panel across that line
slots.fill: panel without a 4 line: cells of colour 1 become the panel's other non-background colour

why: checked on all 4 pairs: 4-line panels are exact mirrors; other panels have 1 replaced by the single other colour

reading: An 8 shape replaces one single-colour component of the patterned grid. Every other component of that same colour with the identical shape (same cells up to translation) is recoloured 8 as well.

new_rows.name: twin
new_rows.datalog:
t8(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 8).
ringc(C) :- t8(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C), C != 8.
srcc(C) :- px(Y, X, C), C != 8, !ringc(C).
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
oy(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ox(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
rel(O, DY, DX) :- obj(O, Y, X), oy(O, A), ox(O, B), DY = Y - A, DX = X - B.
tmpl(T) :- obj(T, Y, X), t8(Y, X).
cand(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), srcc(C).
miss(O, T) :- cand(O), tmpl(T), rel(T, DY, DX), !rel(O, DY, DX).
same(O) :- cand(O), tmpl(T), osize(O, N), osize(T, N), !miss(O, T).
twin(Y, X) :- same(O), obj(O, Y, X).

why: the replaced colour is the one of {0,1,2} absent from the ring around the 8 shape (a maximal component never touches its own colour); every 8-connected component of that colour with the 8 shape's exact shape becomes 8 (key 2->8, 1->8)
invariants: all cells outside the matched components

reading: Some rows hold a 1 cell and, further right, an 8 cell. For each such row take the cells strictly between the 1 and the 8, and stack these strips top to bottom as the output.

slots.unit: per row containing both 1 and 8: the cells strictly between the 1 (left) and the 8 (right)
slots.assemble: strips stacked vertically in input row order (all strips have equal length)

why: each output row equals the between-markers strip of the corresponding marked input row

reading: Partial plus-shaped crosses of 2 lie in a 0/5 noise grid. Each cross is completed to a full plus (arm length taken from the most complete cross in the grid) and the missing cells are painted 8; existing 2s stay.

new_rows.name: cross_gap
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2).
near(Y1, X1, Y2, X2) :- two(Y1, X1), two(Y2, X2), DY = Y2 - Y1, DX = X2 - X1, MY = DY + 3, MX = DX + 3, MY >= 0, MY <= 6, MX >= 0, MX <= 6.
conn(Y1, X1, Y2, X2) :- near(Y1, X1, Y2, X2).
conn(Y1, X1, Y3, X3) :- conn(Y1, X1, Y2, X2), near(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
span(D) :- conn(Y, X1, Y, X2), D = X2 - X1.
span(D) :- conn(Y1, X, Y2, X), D = Y2 - Y1.
maxspan(max(D)) :- span(D).
arm(L) :- maxspan(D), px(L, X, C), D = L + L.
onplus(CY, CX, CY, X) :- arm(L), px(CY, CX, C), two(CY, X), D = X - CX, M1 = D + L, M2 = L - D, M1 >= 0, M2 >= 0.
onplus(CY, CX, Y, CX) :- arm(L), px(CY, CX, C), two(Y, CX), D = Y - CY, M1 = D + L, M2 = L - D, M1 >= 0, M2 >= 0.
stray(CY, CX, Y, X) :- onplus(CY, CX, Y, X), conn(Y, X, Y2, X2), !onplus(CY, CX, Y2, X2).
centre2(CY, CX) :- onplus(CY, CX, Y, X), !stray(CY, CX, Y, X).
cross_gap(CY, X) :- centre2(CY, CX), arm(L), px(CY, X, C), C != 2, D = X - CX, M1 = D + L, M2 = L - D, M1 >= 0, M2 >= 0.
cross_gap(Y, CX) :- centre2(CY, CX), arm(L), px(Y, CX, C), C != 2, D = Y - CY, M1 = D + L, M2 = L - D, M1 >= 0, M2 >= 0.

why: 2-cells cluster (chains of Chebyshev distance <=3) into one cross each; arm L = half the largest same-row/column span inside a cluster (2, or 3 in pair 3); the centre is the unique cell whose plus of arm L holds the whole cluster; its non-2 plus cells become 8

reading: Several 6-coloured shapes each have one single coloured marker cell next to them. Each shape is recoloured with its nearest marker's colour, cropped to its box, and the crops are joined side by side (left to right) when the shapes lie in a row, or stacked (top to bottom) when they lie in a column.

frame.verb: recolour by nearest marker, crop, concatenate

slots.unit: each 6 object (8-connected), cropped to its bounding box
slots.key: colour of the nearest marker cell (non-6 single cell)
slots.assemble: crops concatenated along the axis the shapes are spread on, in input order; markers dropped

why: each output block is a 6 shape's box with 6 replaced by its nearest marker's colour; blocks follow input order

reading: A diagonal run of n 2-cells going up-right is replaced by the next run in the sequence: a run of n+1 cells that starts one step up-right of the old run's upper end and continues up-right; the old run is erased.

slots.subject: the anti-diagonal run of 2 cells (length n)
slots.result: new run of length n+1 starting at (top_y-1, right_x+1), going up-right

why: lengths go 1->2, 2->3, 3->4 and each new run begins diagonally just beyond the previous run's end

reading: A small 8 shape sits in a noisy multi-colour grid. Every placement of that shape, possibly rotated by 90/180/270 degrees, that lies entirely on colour-3 cells is recoloured 8.

new_rows.name: match3
new_rows.datalog:
t8(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 8).
ty(min(Y)) :- t8(Y, X).
tx(min(X)) :- ty(Y), t8(Y, X).
rel(DY, DX) :- t8(Y, X), ty(A), tx(B), DY = Y - A, DX = X - B.
rot(0, DY, DX) :- rel(DY, DX).
rot(1, DX, NY) :- rel(DY, DX), NY = 0 - DY.
rot(2, NY, NX) :- rel(DY, DX), NY = 0 - DY, NX = 0 - DX.
rot(3, NX, DY) :- rel(DY, DX), NX = 0 - DX.
rid(R) :- rot(R, DY, DX).
bad(R, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 3), rot(R, DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !px(Y2, X2, 3).
good(R, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 3), rid(R), !bad(R, Y, X).
match3(Y2, X2) :- good(R, Y, X), rot(R, DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX.

why: cells covered by some rotated copy of the 8 template whose cells are all 3 become 8 (key 3->8); no reflections, no other cells change

reading: Several single-colour shapes; one of them has an 8 cell inside it. Cut out that shape's box and turn the 8 into the shape's own colour.
why: the only multi-coloured component is the shape holding the 8; its box is the output with the 8 cell recoloured to the surrounding shape colour
